  - because: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (starter_groundball_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 59.5%, home 42.6% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,352 batted balls; home over 439 batted balls); a gap of 16.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 11.6 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)
